class.name: NetwDefaultJoin
class.brief_description: The join handler a session falls back to when a game registered none, spawning the joining player at the template the client named.
class.description: Used when a session declared no handler of its own through [method Netw.configure_join]. It puts a joining player into a scene and spawns them at the template the client named, which resolves to a [SpawnSlot]. A client sends [code](scene_stem, spawner_path)[/code] as its join arguments, and those are [method spawn]'s parameters after the [NetwParticipant] every handler takes first. A game wanting a different arrangement declares its own handler with [method Netw.configure_join]. [codeblock] api.session_prepare_join(username, [&"Arena", ^"Player"]) api.multiplayer_peer = peer [/codeblock]

method.name: spawn
method.description: Activates [param scene_stem], resolves the template at [param spawner_path], and adds the node [param participant] plays. The returned promise settles with the entered [NetwSceneHandle]. [param scene_stem] is a declared scene's stem, the name [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_find] answers to, never a [code]res://[/code] path or a [code]uid://[/code] reference. A persistence hydration the player's engine asked for completes before the player is seated, so a returning player enters with its saved state already applied. That hydration is why this answers a promise rather than the handle. See [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_activate] and [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_find]. A game that restores a player to whichever scene it left from registers its own handler with [method Netw.configure_join] and reads that scene itself, because only the game knows where it recorded one. [b]Server Only.[/b]
